## Log
### Saturday 31 October 2026
**9:05 am EDT · Session started.** Goal: review the coding-agent research workflow against public practice and the repo, then set it up. Four Opus research agents launched on non-overlapping lanes.
**9:40 am EDT · Hand-backs: all four research lanes finished.** Main gaps: no findings index, checkpoints and counters enforced only by memory, degrading state files, results without commit stamps. Proposal written and reviewed by the advisor.
**9:55 am EDT · User decision.** Plan approved with corrections (see Needs from you). Setup starts in a pinned Deception-Circuit worktree.
**10:05 am EDT · Planning started.** Feature directory created inside the worktree. Opus planner spawned to write the spec and tickets.
**1:30 pm EDT · Hand-back: plan written.** A binding spec with 25 rulings, 12 tickets in 7 waves, a shared agent brief and a facts report. Its eight open questions were ruled on (session tag format, how to refresh a stale usage reading, which directories the live Codex session still owns, and five smaller ones).
**1:50 pm EDT · Hand-back: independent plan review.** Verdict: approve with nine fixes. The important ones: installing hooks before the tool they call exists could lock a session out of its own tools; the text lint must refuse a bad write before it happens rather than complain after; the migration ticket still touched directories the live Codex session owns. All nine sent back to the planner with rulings. Next: implementation wave A (lint and apply tool; science guards) once the fixes land.
**2:20 pm EDT · Hand-back: text lint and apply tool done and installed.** The lint that refuses glued-together prose and secret-shaped strings now exists, with 68 passing tests across both Python environments. Its first real run found the two glued lines in the memory index and 9 of 13 glued paragraphs in the bad Codex state file, and zero false alarms on clean documents. The apply tool installed the lint into the Alignment repository, switched the three research agent definitions from Sonnet to Opus, updated the usage policy note to the 80% caps, and added the subagent-model default, a one-minute status-line refresh and one-year transcript retention to your Claude settings (backup journal kept). Three more implementers started: the usage gate and freeze logic, the plugin profiles for both tools, and the protocol documents and templates.
**2:35 pm EDT · Hand-back: protocol documents and templates done and installed.** Three guides now live in the Alignment repository's agent docs: how a research session runs (start, delegation, state files, checkpoints, wrap-up), how a synthesis session proposes directions, and how a fresh session audits a past one with eleven checks. Nine templates (start prompt, proposal, worklog, state, ledger, hand-back, audit) live in the Deception-Circuit docs. The hand-back exposed a gap: the tool had no command to create a new direction's files, record GPU reservations, or set worklog header fields. The planner added those three commands to the spec and to the records ticket.
**2:41 pm EDT · Hand-back: plugin profiles done and installed.** Claude defaults now keep superpowers, the tdd and code-review skills, GitHub and the CLAUDE.md helper on, and turn the rest off; four profile files (research, synthesis, writing, audit) switch sets back on per session type. Codex has no true per-profile switch in the installed version, so the bridge prunes the same adapters globally and the writing set is re-enabled by hand when needed (documented in the bridge guide). Turning off shinka and weco in Codex waits for your go because Codex must restart.
**2:55 pm EDT · Hand-back: usage gate core done and installed.** The research-session tool now reads your usage file, tracks session points across weekly resets, decides the freeze and cap rules, and records acknowledgements. Two of your notes landed mid-ticket: the five-hour limit no longer exists on your account, so a missing five-hour reading now means "not applicable" rather than zero; and all times are Eastern. 136 tests pass in both Python environments, and a live check reads the real usage file correctly. Ticket 03 (worklog writer, registry, ledger, findings check) started.

Together they are about 7,700 tokens, against the 60,000 to 80,000 a fresh agent needed before. Eight directions are registered with their status. Two small ledger defects found on the way went back to the tool's implementer. Next: the two migration tickets (handoff standardization and the scripted archive of closed scratch directories) started.
**4:02 pm EDT · Hand-back: hook definitions done; smoke test passed.** The research-session tool now answers every hook event both tools fire: it refuses glued or secret-shaped writes before they happen, blocks new agents and GPU submissions once a usage checkpoint is crossed, reports stale usage readings, counts compactions, and reminds a resumed session where it was. 44 recorded hook exchanges and 252 tests pass in both Python environments, and a live smoke test of every hook command against the installed tool passed. **4:34 pm EDT · Hand-back: pilot checklist and transcript audit command done.** A 13-step pilot checklist now exists, each step with the exact command and the text you should see, plus a table to record pass or fail. **4:47 pm EDT · Hand-back: science guards in the Deception-Circuit code done.** Every new training run and evaluation cell now writes a provenance file beside its results: the code commit, whether the tree was dirty and a hash of the diff, the config hash, the dataset files, the seed, the model revision and a fingerprint of the grader code. A report checker walks a Markdown report and says which numbers resolve to a cited file; on the mechanism-analysis synthesis it resolved 416 of 607 numbers once pointed at the right reports directory, and the unresolved rest are mostly prose repeats and section numbers. A held-out policy and an empty registry exist; the code guard against scoring held-out items is a later ticket. 56 new tests pass in both Python environments, and the full suite shows the same 120 failing names before and after on both interpreters, all of them worktree-only path issues, so no regression. Two findings for later: the repository's root pytest configuration is never loaded by the suite command, so its thread pin does nothing; and the grader fingerprint does not yet cover rubric files in the sibling benchmark checkouts.
**4:47 pm EDT · Process incident P3.** The ticket 04 agent went idle twice without finishing: once at 1:20 pm with its drafts only in scratch and nothing in the worktree, and again at 4:06 pm after launching the final test runs, which it never came back to read. Effect: About 2.5 hours of wall-clock delay on ticket 04; no wrong output. Fix: Orchestrator resumed it once, then wrote the final comparison section itself from the agent's logs. Lesson for the protocol: an agent must not end its turn while a background run it owns is unfinished; it should wait on the run or hand the comparison to the orchestrator explicitly.
**4:48 pm EDT · Cause of the ticket 04 stall found.** The agent twice launched a long test run in the background and ended its turn expecting a completion notice. Subagents in this setup get no such notice, so it sat idle until messaged (1:19 pm to 4:03 pm, then 4:06 pm to 4:45 pm). The orchestrator also accepted the second 'I'll wait' notice at face value. Three fixes go into the wrap-up ticket: a rule that an agent never ends its turn with an unfinished run it owns and waits actively instead; a hook extension that sends an agent back to work when its hand-back status still says pending; and an orchestrator rule that treats a 'waiting' idle notice as a stall.
**5:26 pm EDT · Hand-back: wrap-up ticket done.** Eight findings rows, ten proposed follow-up directions, a two-page handoff and the merge checklist are in the feature folder. The apply tool now plans chained migrations cleanly in a dry run, moves across file systems, and skips writes it applied before. The hook that catches a subagent stopping without a hand-back now also sends it back when the hand-back's status is a placeholder, the fix for the ticket 04 stall. One staged Codex bridge edit from the first ticket had gone stale because the bridge gained hook-trust code since; it is replaced by a one-sentence text edit. 273 research-session tests and 66 tool tests pass in both Python environments.
**5:26 pm EDT · Process incident P4.** The planning agent ran one read-only git command while drafting the plan. Effect: None: the command changed nothing, but agents may not run git at all. Fix: The agent brief forbids every git subcommand for agents, and the orchestrator alone runs git.
